channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: UNICEF Reports Over 2.6 Million Afghan Girls Denied Education Since 2021
item.description: UNICEF announced that over 2.6 million girls in Afghanistan have been denied education since 2021. The restrictions have limited learning opportunities, forcing many girls to stay home after sixth grade. This denial impacts their psychological well-being, increasing feelings of isolation and hopelessness. UNICEF continues to support educational programs for both girls and boys.

item.title: Aybek Aitbekov: 'I Went to America Solely to Become World Champion'
item.description: Aybek Aitbekov, a Greco-Roman wrestler from Astana, won a gold medal at the U23 World Championship in Las Vegas. He expressed immense joy and pride in achieving his dream after extensive training. Aitbekov emphasized that winning for Kazakhstan is a great honor and thanked his coaches and supporters for their contributions to his success.

item.title: Three Dead in East Kazakhstan Region House Fire
item.description: A woman and two children died in a house fire in the village of Bobrovka, East Kazakhstan Region. Firefighters arriving at the scene found the entire building engulfed in flames with the roof collapsed. The cause of the fire is currently under investigation.

item.title: Lower VAT on Vegetables Could Combat Childhood Obesity in Kazakhstan, Says MP
item.description: Kazakh Member of Parliament Askhat Aimagambetov proposes reducing VAT on vegetables to combat childhood obesity, citing international examples. He suggests measures like limiting unhealthy food advertising and adjusting tax policies, noting that awareness campaigns alone are insufficient for dietary change.

item.title: Almaty Facade Renovations Disrupt Small Businesses Amid Ongoing Construction
item.description: Small businesses in Almaty are suffering due to ongoing facade renovations on Soviet-era buildings. Gaukhar Osmonalieva's pet grooming salon and coffee shop, opened in August, faces reduced foot traffic and constant dust from construction. The city launched a large-scale renovation program in 2026, allocating over 25.8 billion tenge for work on 176 buildings, many housing ground-floor businesses.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees 17% Growth in Capital Investments Over Eight Months, Driven by Industry
item.description: Capital investments in Kazakhstan increased by 17% in January-August 2026, with real growth at 8.1% after accounting for price changes, according to Ranking.kz analysts. Industry accounted for over 40% of investments, primarily in manufacturing and mining. The manufacturing sector saw a 39.9% real growth, while the energy sector grew by 49.3%.

item.title: Russia Attacks Ukraine's Energy Infrastructure After US President's 'Energy Truce' Announcement
item.description: Russian forces launched strikes on Kyiv overnight, resulting in casualties and damage to residential buildings and energy infrastructure. The attacks occurred after US President Biden announced an 'energy truce'. Several Ukrainian regions reported damage to energy facilities and civilian infrastructure due to missile and drone strikes.

item.title: Over 15 Million Tenge in Alimony Debt Recovered in East Kazakhstan Region
item.description: In the East Kazakhstan Region, over 15.6 million tenge in alimony debt has been recovered. This follows the prosecution of 19 individuals who evaded child support obligations. Criminal charges were filed in 20 cases, with 15 resulting in convictions. The recovery efforts were prompted by a prosecutor's office investigation into non-payment of child support.

item.title: OIC Envoy Briefs Kabul Diplomats on Afghanistan Visit Outcomes
item.description: The Organization of Islamic Cooperation's Special Envoy to Afghanistan, Ambassador Dr. Tarig Ali Bakheet, briefed ambassadors in Kabul on his recent visit. Discussions focused on humanitarian aid, counter-terrorism, healthcare, education, and livelihood improvements. Bakheet stressed the need for coordinated OIC member state efforts to support Afghanistan's humanitarian and development needs amidst ongoing challenges.

item.title: Kazakhstan Approves Electronic Permit System for Foreign Citizens
item.description: Kazakhstan's government has established rules for an electronic permit system for foreigners entering the country from visa-exempt nations. The system, operational from November 1, 2023, at specific entry points, will expand nationwide by 2027. The electronic permit is valid for 180 days and is free to obtain, with exemptions for certain categories of travelers.

item.title: Kazakhstan People's Council Holds First Regional Forum on Public Ethics
item.description: The Kazakhstan People's Council, chaired by Yerlan Koshanov, held its inaugural regional forum titled 'New Public Ethics: Culture, Morality, Customs' in the West Kazakhstan region. The event, part of implementing presidential directives, gathered over a thousand community representatives, mothers, and experts. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's congratulatory message emphasized the importance of promoting constitutional values, especially among youth.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish 20% Electricity Reserve by 2029
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to create a 20% electricity reserve by 2029, ensuring installed capacity fully covers demand with a necessary buffer. According to the Ministry of Energy, this reserve is crucial for covering potential system failures and reducing reliance on imports. Currently, Kazakhstan's installed capacity is 27.1 GW, with coal generation being the largest component.

item.title: Uzbekistan Recalculates Nearly 800,000 Citizens' Unjustified Utility Debts Totaling 22 Billion Soums
item.description: Uzbekistan's Antimonopoly Committee has recalculated utility debts for nearly 800,000 citizens who were temporarily absent from their primary residences. The committee found discrepancies in subscriber data, leading to unjustified charges. Approximately 800,000 citizens were incorrectly charged for waste removal services, and about 100 for water supply, resulting in a debt adjustment of nearly 22 billion soums.

item.title: Kazakhstan Increases Student Stipends, Questioning Sufficiency for Daily Expenses
item.description: Kazakhstan has been steadily increasing student stipends since 2020, with plans for further hikes by 2025. However, the article questions whether the current stipend amounts are sufficient to cover students' daily expenses, including accommodation, food, and study materials. The government's decree from February 7, 2008, outlines the procedure and amounts for state stipends.

item.title: Hotel in Almaty Previously Owned by Kairat Satybaldy Again Put Up for Auction
item.description: The Double Tree by Hilton Almaty hotel, transferred to state ownership by Kairat Satybaldy, has been re-listed for auction. The Almaty Department of State Property and Privatization is conducting the auction with a starting price of over 38 billion tenge. This follows a previous unsuccessful attempt to sell the hotel.

item.title: Kazakh Man Dies in Prison 20 Days Before Release; Note Blames Management
item.description: A Kazakh man named Yerzhuman, serving time at an Atbasar correctional facility, died by suicide just 20 days before his scheduled release. His sister claims he was forced to clean floors and was placed in solitary confinement after refusing. A note found on his body reportedly read, 'Management is to blame for this.'

item.title: Four More Suspects Detained in Kyzylorda Schoolgirl Rape Case
item.description: Prosecutors in the Kyzylorda region have revealed new details in the investigation of a minor's rape case involving a former sports club coach. The suspect, previously employed by the "Kaysar" club, was dismissed in September 2025, contradicting earlier reports. Relatives of the victim are accused of abducting and assaulting suspects, leading to new criminal cases and arrests.

item.title: International Organizations Urge Kazakhstan to Criminalize Domestic Violence
item.description: UN Committee experts urged Kazakhstan to reform its laws, criminalizing domestic violence as a distinct offense. While Kazakhstan's delegation pledged to adopt such a law, experts question the effectiveness of current measures, noting domestic violence is not yet a separate criminal offense.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Ex-Customs Inspector Awarded Nearly $80,000 for Unlawful Dismissal and Imprisonment
item.description: A former customs inspector in Uzbekistan, sentenced in 2014, has been acquitted and awarded nearly $80,000 in compensation for unlawful dismissal and imprisonment. The Supreme Court reported that the inspector was found guilty of customs violations, forgery, and bribery, serving time until December 2017. He was reinstated to his position with his years of absence counted towards his work record.

item.title: Former HRW Director Warns France's Forced Returns of Afghans Risk Persecution and Torture
item.description: Kenneth Roth, former executive director of Human Rights Watch, stated that France's forced returns of Afghan migrants to Afghanistan put them at risk of persecution and torture. He described the policy as dangerous and conflicting with France's international human rights obligations. An Afghanistan researcher at HRW echoed these concerns.

item.title: Criminal Case Opened in Almaty Over Mass Food Poisoning of Schoolchildren
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated in Almaty following a mass food poisoning incident at the Republican Physics and Mathematics School. Police reported that violations were found in the school's canteen during sanitary-epidemiological inspections. The investigation aims to determine all circumstances and assign legal responsibility for the incident, which hospitalized 48 students.

item.title: Belgian King and Queen Visit Almaty, Explore Nuclear Physics and Equestrian Traditions
item.description: King Philippe and Queen Mathilde of Belgium visited Almaty during a state visit to Kazakhstan. They toured the Institute of Nuclear Physics, learning about cyclotron technology for medical isotopes. The royal couple also experienced Kazakh horse traditions, including archery. Belgium is a major investor in Kazakhstan's economy, with companies in energy, pharmaceuticals, and logistics.

item.title: Trump Announces Start of Mineral Exploration in Greenland
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced that exploration for oil, natural gas, and minerals will soon begin in Greenland. He stated on social media that extensive work is underway, with some experts believing Greenland holds vast, easily accessible oil reserves. Trump emphasized Greenland's strategic importance for US and European defense and security.

item.title: Yandex Data Centers Damaged by Drone Strikes, Affecting Services in Russia and Beyond
item.description: The restoration of three Yandex data centers, damaged by Ukrainian drone strikes, is expected to take months. These incidents caused widespread disruptions for services in Russia and other countries where the tech giant operates. Major companies and users of Yandex services, including ride-hailing, payments, and email, were affected. Russia's government is aware of the difficulties.

item.title: Herat Women Describe Humiliation and Fear Under Taliban Morality Police
item.description: Women and girls in Herat recount deeply distressing experiences with the Taliban's Morality Police, describing humiliation and fear even when adhering to strict dress codes and traveling with a male guardian. They report that encounters, regardless of compliance, leave lasting psychological wounds, anxiety, and restricted freedom, turning life into a 'hell on earth'.

item.title: Uzbek President Signs Law Strengthening Punishment for Violence Against Children
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan has signed a law that increases penalties for violence against children. The legislation introduces amendments to five codes and six laws, including life imprisonment for sexual violence against children under 14 years old.

item.title: Six Officials Detained in Investigation into Deaths of 14 Servicemen in Caspian Sea Incident
item.description: Six officials have been detained as part of the investigation into the deaths of 14 servicemen during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. Kazakhstan's Interior Ministry is investigating potential violations of service negligence and navigation rules. The probe aims to legally assess the actions of all involved personnel.

item.title: National Program for Early Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis Launched in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched a National Program for the early diagnosis of colorectal cancer, part of its state policy on public health and cancer prevention. The initiative involves collaboration with the Association of Oncologists of Uzbekistan, the Republican Specialized Scientific-Practical Medical Center of Oncology and Radiology, and Gustave Roussy International. International experts from the US and UK are participating, conducting masterclasses and seminars in the Andijan region.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Implement Electronic Entry Permits for Foreigners Starting July 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan will require foreigners to obtain an electronic entry permit before arriving in the country, with the new rule taking effect on July 1, 2027. This permit can be obtained for free via a digital platform at least 72 hours before arrival. The system will be phased in starting November 2026.

item.title: SCO Backs Khujand Declaration for Eternal Peace, Citing Central Asian Cooperation
item.description: The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) has endorsed the Khujand Declaration on Eternal Peace, becoming the first international body to do so. SCO Deputy Secretary-General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda highlighted the declaration's importance for strengthening trust and good-neighborly relations in Central Asia, particularly following border agreements between Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Journalist's Widow Urges OSCE to Demand Investigation into Husband's Death
item.description: Natalya Sadykova, widow of slain journalist Aidos Sadykov, appealed to the OSCE to demand a thorough investigation into her husband's killing. Speaking at an OSCE conference, she also highlighted the challenges faced by independent media in Kazakhstan, including digital attacks and politically motivated legal actions against journalists.

item.title: Urbanist Identifies Key Reasons for Persistent Traffic Congestion in Almaty
item.description: Residents of Almaty are expressing frustration over severe traffic jams that occur throughout the day, not just during peak hours. Road repairs and expansion projects on the outskirts, including the route from Aport mall to Kaskelen, are contributing to the gridlock. An urbanist cited the main causes for the city's ongoing traffic problems.

item.title: Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan Can Transform Transit into Joint Production, Analyst Says
item.description: Expanding Central Asia to C6 creates a political basis for closer ties with Azerbaijan, according to analyst Tamilla Mamedova. She believes Uzbekistan sees Azerbaijan as a key link to Europe via the South Caucasus and Turkey. Beyond transit, potential lies in industrial cooperation, processing, and joint investments, particularly along the Middle Corridor.

item.title: Egyptian and Pakistani Foreign Ministers Discuss Regional Issues and Cooperation
item.description: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and Pakistani Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar held a phone call to discuss regional issues and ways to strengthen joint coordination. The ministers also explored methods to ease regional tensions. Their discussion preceded an upcoming meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation foreign ministers.

item.title: Kyiv Hit by Ballistic Missiles, Three Dead and Power Outages Reported
item.description: Kyiv experienced a wave of ballistic missile attacks by Russia, resulting in at least three deaths and over 20 injuries. The city's power supply was disrupted in several districts after energy facilities were hit. President Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine received no prior warning from Western partners about the attacks.

item.title: Tajikistan's Foreign Ministry Expresses Concern Over Attacks in Saudi Arabia
item.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Tajikistan has expressed deep concern regarding recent attacks on Saudi Arabian airports and energy infrastructure. The ministry stated that such actions escalate tensions and hinder peace efforts in the Middle East, urging all parties to cease hostilities and resolve disputes through negotiation.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Departs for CICA Summit in Azerbaijan
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon of Tajikistan has departed for Baku, Azerbaijan, to attend the seventh summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA). He was seen off at Dushanbe International Airport by high-ranking officials. The president is accompanied by several key ministers and advisors.

item.title: Pakistan Border Closure Inflicts Millions in Losses on Afghan Traders
item.description: Afghan traders report millions of dollars in financial losses due to the year-long halt in trade with Pakistan. They have been forced to suspend business activities and reduce staff. Traders face high costs, delays, and spoilage on alternative routes, urging the reopening of Pakistan routes and diversification of transit options.

item.title: Google DeepMind CEO Warns of Major Security Incidents from AI Without Safeguards
item.description: Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind, warns that unchecked AI development could lead to major security incidents within two years if adequate safety measures are not implemented. He described recent AI-related events as "early warnings" from less powerful systems, urging industry, companies, and governments to prioritize AI safety.

item.title: Turkish Authorities Seize Control of Another Opposition TV Channel
item.description: Turkish police raided the offices of opposition TV channel Halk TV, suspending its broadcast and placing it under external administration. The Istanbul Public Prosecutor's Office stated the search is linked to an investigation into the chairman of Halk TV's board, accused of bid rigging, bribery, and money laundering. The channel's chairman called the move politically motivated.
